Does explain the two axes ('OutOfSync is a desired-vs-live manifest diff… Degraded is a resource health verdict') but never identifies the stated statuses on an object.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved

expectations.text: Checks metric results and measurements in the AnalysisRun

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations

expectations.text: Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details

expectations.text: Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
expectations.evidence: Full spec.generators git block: repoURL https://github.com/alimobrem/agentit-gitops, revision HEAD, directories path apps/* and exclude apps/agentit.

expectations.text: Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected

expectations.text: Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)
expectations.evidence: 'The generator pattern apps/* requires at least one path segment under apps/, so apps does not match'; ranks branch/HEAD mismatch and empty directories, rules out repo access and explicitly rules out the exclude rule as a red herring.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: `oc get applicationsets.argoproj.io agentit-managed-apps -o json | jq .spec` → 'No spec.strategy, therefore the default AllAtOnce applies'.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: Only generic: 'Each steps[].matchExpressions selects on labels of the generated Application… If spec.template.metadata.labels doesn't stamp env: production, the production step matches zero apps.' No actual step group identified.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Lists 'maxUpdate too small or zero. maxUpdate: 0 means unlimited' and the Healthy+Synced gate as checks, but no actual maxUpdate or health-gate state is examined (no such object).

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: 'Check status.applicationStatus[] for the straggler and which step it is attributed to'; verifies on the live object that 'status has only conditions and health — no applicationStatus array at all', and states one app stuck Progressing or Degraded 'blocks the whole wave indefinitely'.

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: 'RollingSync advances only when every Application in the current step is Healthy and Synced. One app stuck Progressing, or Synced+Degraded, blocks the whole wave indefinitely — there is no timeout.'

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Root cause verified on-cluster ('progressive syncs are disabled' — ARGOCD_APPLICATIONSET_CONTROLLER_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_SYNCS absent from the deployment env, argocd-cmd-params-cm and the ArgoCD CR), with a 'Proposed fix' enabling the flag plus the GitOps Promoter alternative.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: `oc get rollout bluegreen-demo -o json | jq .spec.strategy` showing activeService, previewService, autoPromotionEnabled true, autoPromotionSeconds 30.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: 'autoPromotionEnabled: false means "wait for a human", full stop. It is not "wait for analysis to decide"… nothing will ever clear it except an explicit kubectl argo rollouts promote.'

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: 'There is no prePromotionAnalysis and no postPromotionAnalysis anywhere in the spec. Neither block exists.' plus `oc get analysisruns -l rollouts-pod-template-hash=<previewHash>` to distinguish 'analysis is failing' from 'analysis never ran'.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: `oc get svc -n example-rollout` lists bluegreen-active and bluegreen-preview; activeSelector==previewSelector==5c698fbc89; fix list says 'verify previewService has endpoints and that activeService/previewService both exist'.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: 'Unlike canary — where an analysis entry in steps[] makes the gate obvious — blue-green runs analysis only if strategy.blueGreen.prePromotionAnalysis.templates[] is populated.'

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis (manual hold + no analysis configured; prePromotionAnalysis only runs when autoPromotionEnabled is true) with three alternative 'Proposed fix (not executed)' paths.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocd -A` returns three CRs, corroborated by three distinct routes.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Table of Instance / Namespace / Scope / Apps / AppSet ctrl / Rollouts / Route TLS for all three, plus their route hostnames.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: 'Working through all three instances…' with per-instance scope evidence (cluster-config namespaces, destination secrets, managed-by labels) and instance-specific findings 3 and 5.

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: 'Answer to "which instance?" — None of them individually — the fault is shared infrastructure', with the multi-instance Application-registration ambiguity spelled out at the end.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance
expectations.evidence: Per-instance comparison table plus instance-scoped findings (stray argocd instance in openshift-gitops-operator; team-b insecure edge route) alongside the cross-instance findings.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: 'No namespace finance, no Application billing-service. The only Application is team-b-gitops/team-b-guestbook (Synced/Healthy, not Suspended)' — Suspended is never identified on a real object.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: 'Argo CD health status Suspended… is a first-class, healthy status in Argo CD's health model — not an error', listing CronJob spec.suspend, paused Deployment/Rollout, BlueGreenPause, suspended Job.

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource to identify what is suspended and why
expectations.evidence: Gives the resource-walk one-liner over status.resources[] printing kind/name/health to 'find the culprit', and notes 'If a paused Rollout is the cause, the app is working as designed and the right move is to promote the Rollout'.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: 'Why I'd push back on "the team thinks it's broken": All three causes above are intended states… The remediation is almost always "explain the schedule" or "promote the rollout", not a repair.'

expectations.text: Produces a report distinguishing intentional suspension from a genuine problem
expectations.evidence: 'Nothing in Argo CD's health model treats Suspended as a failure — Degraded is the failure status', while separately flagging the genuine defect (sync windows with no manualSync/timeZone).

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: Correctly determines the only Application is single-source ('spec.source (singular, Kustomize) — no spec.sources', 'status.sourceType: Kustomize — singular; no status.sourceTypes array'); no multi-source Application exists, so none is detected.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Step 1 python one-liner enumerating index, repoURL, chart/path, targetRevision and ref for every entry of spec.sources, with helm.valueFiles / $values wiring covered in the failure-mode list.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: No live object to diagnose; supplies a strong isolation method (status.sourceTypes length as the first missing index, syncResult.revisions per source, conditions naming the repoURL, repo-server logs filtered by host) but names no failing source.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Keys everything off the per-source ordinal ('Index the sources — the ordinal is how everything else is keyed') and compares sourceTypes array length against spec.sources.

expectations.text: Produces a report identifying the specific failing source and the fix
expectations.evidence: 'Nothing to fix — the Application does not exist.' Report gives ranked failure modes and cluster-specific caveats (AppProject sourceRepos restriction, no repository secrets) but no specific failing source or concrete fix.
